reviews.comment: Professor Hamilton is a genuine person who doesn't like to see his student fail. People give him flak for the test/material, but that's just the curriculum that he has to teach - its a mess regardless of who you take. In any case, he is a great prof because he actually gave us Arduinos and hardware to apply what we learned in class (good fun).

His lectures arent organized but thats every intro to engr prof. His wife convinced him to put grades in 5 buckets where a 0-20% in the class curved to 50-60%, 20-40% curved to 60-70%, etc. (W wife). He realized all of his kids were failing the final too and gave us a huge curve while the other 216 profs didn't care their students failed.

There are quizzes before every class over the lecture slides which have nothing do with the homework. His lectures are completely worthless also. The TA's graded the lab unfairly hard, but that may or may not be related to him as a teacher. If he's one of your only options then choose him, but we definitely had more work than other classes.
reviews.ratingTags: Tough grader--EXTRA CREDIT--Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment: Dr. Hamilton was not the professor for me. Homework was nothing like lecture. He called me out in class for "emailing him too much" and I left his office hours crying one day. Some people liked him, but I felt like I could not learn in that environment at all. If you like teaching yourself, you may be fine.

Hamilton is the definition of mid. Lectures weren't very helpful when doing the homework and the pre-class quizzes were just annoying. Honors project was actually cool though, and basically everyone got a 100. Final wasn't too bad either, if you study you will be fine.

He is hilarious and always makes the lecture entertaining. Also, he tries to make students get involved with the class. However, I understand that he is in a hurry because of the holidays, but the lectures go so fast that I cannot keep up. Be sure to read his slides before class, although his slides don't help much with homework.

did make some questionable jokes and comments over the semester; lectures and HWs are pretty connected but have nothing to do with the lab which is most of the grade; final is really hard so do good on the labs

PHYS 217 during Fall Semester. Prof Hamilton was passionate during lectures. PowerPoint slides are provided that contain information applicable to the homework assignment and the final. An Arduino project was assignment that allowed for us to learn C++ and how to collect data. Provided an amazing review for the final. Very helpful in office hours.

His lectures are kind of irrelevant and won't help for the weekly hws/labs. I went to my TA's office hrs to get help on the hw, since they tend to be poorly worded & confusing. Overall, Hamilton is a nice prof (esp if you go to office hrs) and you can do well in his class fairly easily. Not much hw given and the final was very fair and reasonable.

Lectures are useless and do not help me with the HW at all! He also talks about things that have nothing to do with what we're doing in class which is just a waste of my time. I would appreciate it if he goes over examples similar to the HW problems and explain things in detail instead of rushing through the lectures. Would not recommend.
reviews.ratingTags: Lots of homework--Accessible outside class--Participation matters

reviews.comment: Hamilton is a really cool, funny guy and I really enjoyed being in his class. The lectures were short and straight forward, labs werent too hard. Some homeworks and the final were tough for me because I took phys 1 at a community college and I forgot a lot of the material. But if youre taking 206 at TAMU you should be good.

Lectures are covered incredibly fast and he does have some dated views. But he is passionate and you can feel his excitement during office hours. He is fair in that he will continue explaining as long as you keep asking questions. The honors project is ez. Just make sure to not fall behind. Ask questions. Concepts are hard.

Overall, not a bad pick. However, he does make some comments in lecture that are unnecessary. He goes through lecture material really quickly and I didn't learn too much from it. The lab TAs grade really hard, but he can't control that. Fair grader and offers a decent bit of extra credit. Honors project is pretty easy and the final is reasonable.

I don't know why he doesn't have higher ratings but I really like professor Hamilton! He really cares about his students and actually tries to make lectures interesting. The homework assignments are very straightforward and he's more than willing to help you out when you need it. Definitely recommend taking his class!
Rude

The right-winged Hamilton does not care about your grades. He may pretend to be a classical university liberal Associate Professor who seems to be inclusive and cares about diversity, but in fact he does not. Underneath his mask lies hypocrisy. He will force his views upon you. If you do not agree with him, well, good luck getting an A.
reviews.ratingTags: Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.--Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment: Solid prof for ENGR 216/217. He makes his lectures interesting with real life examples and jokes, and obviously enjoys teaching. There is fairly easy, open-note homework each week, which is just enough for this class. Only downside is attendance is recorded, but it makes up a relatively small portion of your grade.
reviews.ratingTags: Respected--Skip class? You won't pass.--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: I took the honors section, and the only difficult portion of the course was the lab portion. It's graded by TA's which he (and you) have no control over, and they grade rough. The honors project (the only difference from the normal class) is very simple, and he's willing to help you at every step of the way. Just pay attention during lectures
Very nice and smart guy. Explains everything really well and is a pretty funny guy. Would def recommend. Don't understand why he does not have a higher rating.
reviews.ratingTags: Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class--Participation matters

reviews.comment: Honestly a really good professor and I'm surprised his ratings are as low as they are. The key to this class is going to his office hours. He will help you in-depth on the homeworks and explains concepts exceptionally well. Really cares about his students. 1 weekly hw and it's usually not too time-consuming. Overall recommend taking his class.

Peter is weird. Some of the things that come out of his mouth are just weird and a little awkward. He rushed thru the class content at lightning speed and always assigned hw when a lot of other 217 classes don't have weekly hw that's a page long. That being said he does care about his students and discussed factual COVID info with us in class.

This class is poorly designed and the labs can sometimes be confusing and unclear. A lot of the grade will depend on the grading of the TA on the labs. Dr. Hamilton is a great person though. Sometimes forces jokes too hard and it can be awkward. Cares about students and is very available outside of class. Very willing to teach and assist.

As a human he is tolerable. I took ENGR 217 because Texas A&M requires me as an Engineer to take this class. The class is already a waste of my time and life energy. Some profs are cool and realize its a big prank and is an excuse for the university to get more money. This man takes his job way to seriously and can unintentionally be a jerk.

not a very nice guy. he treats his students pretty poorly. weekly homework as well, which you cant even solve from the notes provided. he expects us to known information beyond the scope of the course. he needs to chill out

Excellent. Lectures are well-formed. Challenges you as an engineer, gives helpful tips on navigating the workplace. Likes to engage the whole class, so don't expect to go unnoticed by sitting in the back! Helpful during office hours, truly cares about the student. He sometimes runs out of time during lectures, but his slides are available online.

We have yet to finish a single presentation in his class, leaving us to self study the back half of every week's topic. He really has good intentions, and I respect him for that, but ENGR 216 as a whole is a complete shot in the dark. If you do well on labs (70% of your grade for non-honors) you'll be fine, but the weekly HW tends to be annoying.
reviews.ratingTags: Gives good feedback--Lots of homework--Group projects

reviews.comment: Dr. Hamilton had good intentions to assign the class a project coding with a motherboard that would lead to building a rover similar to the one many students did in 111. The problem is that the program we used crashed plenty of times and the project became exceptionally harder than it should that he would eventually give the class a huge curve.
reviews.ratingTags: Lots of homework--Skip class? You won't pass.--Group projects

reviews.comment: Dr. Hamilton is a pretty good lecturer and I enjoyed his classes. The subject matter was interesting and our project was fun, although somewhat painful at times. The tests were quite difficult. A third of the grade was homework, which were free points if you actually did it. I definitely recommend Dr. Hamilton if you enjoy the subject.
reviews.ratingTags: Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.--Caring

reviews.comment: Dr. Hamilton does not care about your performance in the class. The first few weeks, I tried to ask him questions and he would vaguely answer them. The presentations couldn't help walk me through the class. He just could not get me back on track in the class. Overall, made me lose some interest in engineering.
reviews.ratingTags: Participation matters--LOTS OF HOMEWORK--BEWARE OF POP QUIZZES

reviews.comment: Not as bad a prof as people make him out to be. He's very intelligent and knows the engineering world. Even though he may seem to come across as quirky and uninformed on the course, his industry experience is priceless and will help you get a job in the real world. If you take the time to ask him for help in class, he'll help you.
Pete doesn't do well to let you know what's expected of you and his lectures are less than helpful

Gives lots of homework especially for a 2 credit hour classes but sometimes pushes deadlines back. Often makes RAT's worth many points to boast your grade. Just beware he gets off topic and random when he lectures and doesn't use a mic despite him not speaking loud enough.

Very sweet professor, often pushes back deadlines, and RATs are often announced (if not, just expect them always after zybook readings!), thus far no CFUs which is really nice most people I know have either an A or a high B. This time was his first time teaching 111 so it was messy at first, but got way better. An A is definitely possible
